title: edikt phasea verify receipt
description: Written by `edikt phasea verify --plan <id>` at .edikt/state/phasea/<plan_id>.receipt.json. Records, per item, whether the sidecar-extractor's dispatch produced schema-valid, freshly-pinned output. A receipt with consumed:true is terminal: `phasea verify` MUST refuse to re-verify or re-consume the same plan_id again (exit 2). verified_at is one of two runtime-state timestamps in the phasea contract family (the other is the journal's ts); the PLAN artifact carries none — it alone is bound by ADR-020 byte-determinism.

schema_version.description: Contract version for this receipt file's on-disk shape. Bumped 1 → 2 by SPEC-013's Amendment of 2026-09-02 (the `stalled` status); bumped 2 → 3 alongside the plan schema to add per-item extractor_model / extractor_contract. Integer, matching the plan schema's convention — see phasea-dispatch-plan.v3.schema.json's schema_version description.

plan_id.description: The plan this receipt verifies against. Matches exactly one phasea-dispatch-plan.v2 file's plan_id.

items.description: One entry per item in the referenced plan. A receipt always covers every planned item — there is no partial receipt that silently omits an item, because an omitted item would be indistinguishable from one that was never checked (INV-013).

item_id.description: Matches the item_id of the corresponding entry in the plan this receipt verifies.

status.description: The per-item verify outcome. "ok" — expected_output.path exists, parses as YAML, validates against gov-sidecar.v2, and its artifact_sha256 matches what was pinned in the plan (parent-hash check passed). "output-missing" — expected_output.path does not exist on disk. "schema-invalid" — the file exists and parses but fails gov-sidecar.v2 validation. "parent-hash-mismatch" — the keystone check: artifact_path's on-disk sha256 no longer equals the plan's pinned artifact_sha256, so whatever the extractor read cannot be proven to be the planned version. "prompt-version-mismatch" — the installed extractor's resolved prompt_version (ADR-055) no longer matches the plan item's pinned prompt_version, meaning the extraction contract changed between planning and verify. "failed-terminal" — this item has been re-verified attempts >= phasea.max_attempts_per_item times while still not ok, and the skill MUST NOT re-dispatch it again; the plan as a whole stays unconsumed and Phase B is refused (AC-013-3) until a human intervenes and a fresh plan is computed. "pins-unrestorable" — D6's restore step (`edikt phasea restore`) could not reinstate a mandatory pinned field (e.g. `human_approved_at`) that the pre-dispatch pin-set captured on a prior sidecar, because the regenerated sidecar's shape no longer admits it or the field's prior value cannot be reconciled with the new content. Distinct from "failed-terminal": failed-terminal is a retry-exhaustion state reached after repeated re-verification, while pins-unrestorable is terminal on FIRST observation — a lost pin is never eligible for another restore attempt against the same plan_id (INV-015: governance content, including a human's prior approval, must never leave silently, and squashing this into failed-terminal would let a retry-budget count stand in for a permanent, human-visible loss). "length-exceeded" — the sidecar parses and its anchors may be entirely valid, but one or more directives[].text / prohibitions[].text exceed gov-sidecar.v2's 500-character maxLength. Split out of "schema-invalid" because it has a known mechanical remedy the extractor prompt already carries (sidecar-extractor.md:742 — split at the natural seam, reusing the same source_excerpts), so a targeted correction pass resolves it without re-extracting. Retryable. "anchor-invalid" — the sidecar parses and validates against the schema, but one or more anchors do not quote the parent byte-exactly. Also split out of "schema-invalid": the remedy is to re-quote those spans. Retryable. These two exist because collapsing them into "schema-invalid" made "split four sentences" indistinguishable from "re-extract everything" — measured on guideline-event-transport, which had 83 VALID anchors and failed only on length. "diverged" — attempt N produced MORE defects on the same axis than attempt N-1. Terminal, and reached BEFORE the retry budget is exhausted: a retry that is getting worse will not improve by being run again. Distinct from "failed-terminal" ("budget spent") — "diverged" means the budget was deliberately NOT spent. "stalled" — the dispatcher reported the subagent ended without a result (stream watchdog, kill, crash) and nothing is on disk; retryable like output-missing and distinct from it on purpose (SPEC-013 SR-013). Assigned only from the caller's `--stalled` report and never when output exists: the output is the evidence, the report is not. "lossless-loss" — the item is a lifted sidecar (plan reason stale-migration-preserved) and the output dropped or rephrased a directive the pre-dispatch pin snapshot carried under migration_preserved; the extractor no longer sees that baseline, so the proof lives here, against the snapshot. Retryable — the remedy is a re-dispatch with the migrate-time suffix — and `phasea verify --on-loss=accept` passes the item with the loss written to `diagnostic`. "lossless-unmeasured" — the snapshot carried no baseline to compare against; nothing was measured, so nothing passed (INV-013). Retryable.

attempts.description: How many times `phasea verify` has evaluated this item against this plan_id. Increments at verify time, not at dispatch time (owner-recommended: simpler than introducing a separate claim verb). An item already at status "ok" in a prior receipt for the same plan_id is carried forward unchanged on a later verify call — its attempts value does not increment further, because it is no longer re-evaluated.

diagnostic.description: WHY this item is not ok, in a form the next dispatch can act on. Present exactly when status is not "ok". THIS FIELD IS THE POINT OF THE CONTRACT: before it existed the diagnostic was computed by verify and held only in memory (VerifyOutcome.Details), while the retry in commands/gov/compile.md reads THIS receipt — so a re-dispatch resent the identical prompt with no knowledge that it had failed or why. An unseeded retry draws its second sample from the same distribution as the first, which is why the measured case regressed from 1 over-cap directive to 4 rather than converging.

defect_axis.description: WHICH KIND of defect, so a retry can be steered rather than merely repeated. "length" and "anchor" have known mechanical remedies; "schema" and "parse" do not and must not be retried as if they did (a parse error that names its line is the exception: its correction_prompt names the line). "overclaim" — verify_kind behavioral asserted without both fixture files; its correction_prompt restates the kind-by-shape rule. defect_count is only comparable between attempts sharing an axis.

defect_count.description: Number of defects on defect_axis. The quantity convergence is measured on: a fall between attempts is improvement, a rise is divergence.

anchors_valid.description: Anchors that quote the parent byte-exactly. Recorded on EVERY outcome including a pure length failure, because "83 valid anchors, 4 over-cap texts" is a different instruction than "83 broken anchors".

anchors_broken.description: Anchors that do not quote the parent byte-exactly.

anchors_whitespace_only.description: The part of anchors_broken whose quote carries the parent's words with reconstructed whitespace (a re-wrapped or re-indented quote): the correction_prompt hands each one the parent's exact bytes, so a copy fixes it. The remainder of anchors_broken is spliced, misnumbered or not in the parent at all. Absent when zero or not measured.

needs_review.description: How many directives and prohibitions on the sidecar carry needs_review: true, counted by verify on the file for every item it measured (ok, or classified on a defect axis — a quarantined write is counted on its quarantine copy). Reports quote this count, never the extractor's own narration. Absent when zero or not measured.

convergence.description: This attempt compared against the previous one on the same defect_axis. A retry policy that cannot detect divergence keeps paying for it. "unknown" — the two attempts failed on DIFFERENT axes, or this outcome had no sidecar to measure; a length count and an anchor count are different quantities and their difference is meaningless. Deliberately NOT treated as divergence: an unmeasurable comparison is not evidence of getting worse.

correction_prompt.description: The instruction the next dispatch MUST carry, rendered at verify time and persisted so the retry reads one artifact instead of re-deriving the diagnostic from a tree that may have changed. Empty when the axis admits no mechanical correction, so a caller cannot send an empty instruction and count it as a seeded retry.

extractor_model.description: Present only when status is "ok": the model that actually performed this item's extraction, stamped onto the sidecar itself in the same verify call via sidecar.InsertKeyInPlace. A validated --extractor-model self-report from the dispatching context takes precedence (the only source that can be right under extractor.model: inherit); otherwise the installed frontmatter's own model: pin (correct for an explicit config value); otherwise the literal "unrecorded", never a guess.

extractor_contract.description: Present only when status is "ok": hex SHA-256 of the resolved extractor agent definition's exact bytes at verify time, stamped onto the sidecar alongside extractor_model. Distinguishes two extractions sharing a prompt_version but not a body.

consumed.description: True only when every item in `items` has status "ok". Setting this true is the one irreversible transition in the phasea contract: once true, this plan_id MUST be rejected by any further `phasea verify --plan <id>` invocation (exit 2), whether or not the underlying corpus later changes. A receipt with consumed:false and every remaining item at failed-terminal or pins-unrestorable represents a terminal state — also never eligible for Phase B, but distinct from CONSUMED because it never becomes eligible again for this plan_id; recovery requires a fresh plan (a corpus or config change that produces a new plan_id).

verified_at.description: ISO8601 UTC timestamp of this verify run. Runtime state, not a compiled governance surface — exempt from ADR-020's byte-determinism rule, which binds rendered/compiled output, not audit timestamps on state files.
